title: PanoramaSkyMaterial Wraps Around Top and Bottom of Scene by 1 Texel with Filtering On
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproduceable In: v4.6.stable.steam [89cea1439]

### System information

Windows 11 - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 - AMD Ryzen 9 5900X 12/24-Core Processor - 32 GB RAM

### Issue description

This is a pretty minor bug because it's nearly impossible to notice with a proper high-res environment map, but I wanted to report it all the same.

Basically, when you set up a PanoramaSkyMaterial in your WorldEnvironment, supply it with a texture, and turn Filtering on, the very top texel of the sky in the scene will wrap around to the bottom of the texture and the very bottom texel of the sky in the scene will wrap around to the top of the texture.

This is almost impossible to notice with a proper high-res HDR background texture; I only noticed it because I'm in the process of making my own and the testing texture I had rendered was at a MUCH lower resolution. Even with a texture resolution of only 1024x512 for the background the top and bottom wraparound in the scene are just tiny faded circles only a few pixels wide, only noticeable if the camera is ever allowed to look almost directly straight up or straight down.

If there was a way internally to have the sky texture UV coordinates clamp to V but repeat U, that would likely be the best solution. I don't know enough about the internals to know if that's possible.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a WorldEnvironment node to a 3D scene.
2. Set its background to "Sky" and create a new Sky resource for it.
3. Create a new "PanoramaSkyMaterial" for the Sky resource and set its texture to any low-res texture where the top row of pixels are a distinctly different colour from the bottom row of pixels. (The higher the vertical resolution of the texture, the harder this will be to notice.)
4. Turn "Filter" on for the Sky.
5. Rotate the 3D view to look almost directly up or directly down to see the spots which are bleeding over between the top and bottom of the texture in the sky.

N/A
